messages.subject: Re: questions about a Shiny app using dynamic UI and reactiveValues
parts:
You actually don't need reactiveValues() at all if all you want is caching. Reactive expressions already have caching built-in. So in other words:

dataInput <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$file))
    return(NULL)
  return(read.csv(input$file$datapath))
})

You can call dataInput() all over your code, and read.csv will only be executed a single time for each file that is uploaded.

To answer your original question anyway, reactive expressions (i.e. reactive({ ... }) ) should never be used to ASSIGN variables, whether reactive variables or non-reactive variables. You don't want them to have side effects because, as you've discovered, reactive expressions don't execute unless they are needed by an output or observer. The right way to assign variables in response to inputs/reactives changing, is to write an observer.

You can find out much more about observers and the rest in the Reactivity Overview.


On Sat, May 25, 2013 at 9:47 AM, Stéphane Laurent <lauren...@yahoo.fr> wrote:

I'm doing a Shiny applications with some dynamic UI. In the first tab, the user uploads a file and choose the columns to be plotted. 

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/testDynamicUIdataplot/

An example csv data file is attached.

I encounter two problems:

- When uploading the file, a temporary error message appears, like :

Error in names(dat) <- ...
  'names' attribute [4] must be the same length as the vector [0]
  
  I'm under the impression this is a "synchronization" problem of the reactive process and the R code. Surely I could suppress this error message with the `try()` function, but is there a better way to solve this problem ?
  
- I misunderstand the practice of `reactiveValues()`. I'm trying to use `reactiveValues()` in order to store the loaded data in a R object, to avoid reading several times the csv file (for instance if I call the data with my `dataInput()` function the at each time it reads the csv file).  
My `reactiveValues()` object is called `DATA`, it contains the two objects `dat0` and `dat`. I have noticed that I can directly call `DATA$dat0` but not `DATA$dat` (thus each time I want to get `DATA$dat` I call my function `wdatGet()`). Is it related to the fact that `dat0` appears in the output, but not `dat` ? 
More importantly, could you please comment about the way to use `reactiveValues()` in order to store the loaded csv file ? Or maybe there's a more appropriaté way than using `reactiveValues` ?

``` 
# setwd("~/Work/RD/QC Charts")
## server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  ##
  ## load data file
  ##
  fileInput <- reactive( {
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    input$file
  })
  ##
  ## output message : file loaded
  ##
  output$loaded <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return("no file loaded yet")
    }
    ""
  })
  ##
  ## output : show loaded file
  ##
  output$filetable <- renderTable({
    fileInput()
  })
  ##
  ## read data file
  ##
  DATA <- reactiveValues()
  dataInput <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    inFile <- input$file
    dat0 <- read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=T)
    DATA$dat0 <- dat0
    dat0
  })
  ##
  ## output: print contents of loaded file
  ##
  output$dat <- renderTable({
    dataInput()
  })
  ##
  ## Variables selection 
  ##
  output$select_date <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    factors <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) == "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(factors) %in% c("date", "time")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), factors[which(ok)[1]], factors[1]) 
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.date',
                label = "Select date:",
                choices = factors,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$datelabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("datelabel", "x-axis label:", value=input$col.date)
  })
  output$select_group <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    factors <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) == "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(factors) %in% c("tech")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), factors[which(ok)[1]], factors[1]) 
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.group',
                label = "Select coloring group:",
                choices = factors,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$legend <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("legend", "Legend title:", value=input$col.group)
  })
  output$select_LP <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("lp", "cp1")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[1]) 
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.LP',
                label = "Select low control:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$LPlabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("LPlabel", "y-axis label for low control:", value=input$col.LP)
  })
  output$select_HP <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("hp", "cp2")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[2]) 
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.HP',
                label = "Select high control:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$HPlabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("HPlabel", "y-axis label for high control:", value=input$col.HP)
  })
  output$select_calibration <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("range", "reference", "calibration")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[1]) 
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.calibration',
                label = "Calibration indicator:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  ##
  ## create dataframe with generic variable names 
  ##
  wdatGet <- reactive({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)){ return(NULL) }
    if(input$calibration){
        dat <- subset(dat, select=c(input$col.date,input$col.LP,input$col.HP,input$col.calibration,input$col.group))
        names(dat) <- c("Date", "LP", "HP", "calib", "group")
        dat$pch <- 19
        if(all(dat$calib) %in% c(0,1)){
          dat[which(dat$calib==1),"pch"] <- 23
        }
    }else{
        dat <- subset(dat, select=c(input$col.date,input$col.LP,input$col.HP,input$col.group))
        names(dat) <- c("Date", "LP", "HP", "group")
        dat$pch <- 19
    }
    dat$color <- as.numeric(dat$group)
    dat$mydate <- as.Date(dat[,"Date"], "%d/%m/%Y") 
    dat$dateID <- as.numeric(dat$mydate)
    f <- switch(input$transfo, none=function(x) x, log=log)
    dat <- transform(dat, LP=f(LP), HP=f(HP))
    dat <- droplevels(subset(dat, subset= !is.na(LP) & !is.na(HP) & !is.na(date)))
    DATA$wdat <- dat
  })
  ####
  #### PLOT DATA 
  ####
  output$plotdata <- renderPlot({
    wdatGet()
    dat <- DATA$wdat
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
        # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    d <- dat$mydate 
    x <- dat$LP
    y <- dat$HP
    k <- 1.08 # factor for ylim (default =1.08)
    par(mfrow=c(2,1),mar=c(6,3,3,3))
    r <- x
    ylims <- (max(r)-diff(range(r))/2) + c(-1,1) * diff(range(r)) * k/2 
    plot(d,x,type="p",xaxt="n", 
         xlab=NA, ylab="LP", 
         col=dat$group, 
         ylim=ylims,
         pch=dat$pch,bg="gold")
    at <- seq(d[1], d[length(d)], length.out=25)
    axis.Date(1, at = at,
              labels = at,
              format= "%d/%m/%Y", las = 2)
    r <- y
    ylims <- (max(r)-diff(range(r))/2) + c(-1,1) * diff(range(r)) * k/2 
    plot(d,y,type="p",xaxt="n", 
         xlab=NA, ylab="LP", 
         col=dat$group, 
         ylim=ylims,
         pch=dat$pch,bg="yellow2")
    axis.Date(1, at = at,
              labels = at,
              format= "%d/%m/%Y", las = 2)
  },  height=800)
})
```
